text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were expected to continue trading in dull ranges early next week after spending much of Friday drifting at lower levels. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.33, down 0.30 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts closed higher, extending Thursday's gains, as investors scaled back their expectations of an imminent rise in interest rates. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-31/32, up 07/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond future slipped slightly but ended off lows. Traded in narrow range, recovered after initial sell-off on U.S. production data. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.46, down 0.16 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt futures forged another all-time high on the March contract on LIFFE after a week of steady gains. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.28, up 0.29 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries edged higher at mid-morning amid expectations that the Federal Reserve would not raise rates soon. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-28/32, up 05/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.83 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures ended lower on fears of possible selling by life insurers. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 125.69, down 0.49 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - New issues activity calmed ahead of the weekend but the market still notched up a benchmark.

Ten German states formally launched their widely touted 4.5 billion mark ($2.8 billion) 10-year jumbo bond at a 15.5 basis points spread over Bunds. The states stipulated the reoffer yield be no more than 16 basis poinst. Dealers said that spread was too tight and with Friday's offering having less of an international flavour than a prior laender jumbo, the issue quickly traded down to full fees. ($1=1.6040 Mark)
